newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia palm oil exports to Pakistan seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia palm oil exports to Pakistan seen falling.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil exports to Pakistan are likely to fall in the coming months following the latest devaluation of the Pakistani rupee, which makes imports more expensive, traders said on Wednesday.
However, the extent of the reduction in imports would depend on the supply-demand situation in Pakistan, they said.

"The imports depend on the supply-demand situation," a dealer said. "Right now there is sufficient stock in the country and the Pakistanis do not need to buy oil. So they don't have to worry about the devaluation."
The State (central) Bank Of Pakistan on Tuesday devalued the rupee 3.79 percent to 36.9700/37.1549 to the dollar from 35.6200/35.7981 fixed on August 29.

Latest available official data from the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority showed Malaysian palm oil imports by Pakistan, the second largest buyer of the country's palm oil in 1995, were 461,311 tonnes in January-May this year against 371,769 tonnes in the same period of last year.
Traders in Pakistan said last week that domestic vegetable oil prices were expected to remain unchanged this week with the local market amply stocked.
"We expect a slight rise in vegoil rates abroad, but prices in the local market will remain stable due to the good stock position," a dealer in Pakistan said.
"The arrival of cotton seed is also likely to start by the end of this month, which will hold the local prices steady."
Pakistan's vegetable oil stocks rose to 160,000 tonnes last week from 156,000 tonnes in the previous week.
Cargo surveyor Societe Generale de Surveillance (SGS) Malaysia Sdn Bhd said Pakistan was estimated to have bought 129,661 tonnes of Malaysian palm oil in August, down from 140,141 tonnes in July.
Pakistan's Ghee Corporation had booked 9,000 tonnes of RBD palm oil by September 7, and another 9,000 tonnes by October 10.
Traders said Pakistani importers would use up available stocks before considering buying again.
RBD palm olein is now quoting at $562.50 a tonne FOB Malaysia for October and $550 for November/December.
Dealers said RBD palm oil and palm olein stocks remained steady at 125,000 tonnes compared with the previous week. Soyoil and sunflower oil stocks rose to 27,000 tonnes from 20,000.
